Here are the main Spain stories from mid-October 2026, based on the search results:

**Snap election and housing crisis**
- Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called an early general election for 29 November. Congress rejected two housing decrees put forward by his government. The vote came after parliament rejected measures intended to quell public anger and mass protests over the country's housing crisis.
- The protests began when an 87-year-old woman was evicted from her home. The eviction sparked nationwide protests. Sanchez then put two housing decrees before parliament, but both were rejected.
- Parties are now forming alliances ahead of the vote. One report says left-wing divisions persist and housing remains a central issue.

**Corruption cases**
- Sánchez's wife, Begoña Gómez, faces accusations over her university role. She is accused of using her position as the prime minister's wife to advance her career at Madrid's Complutense University. Gomez denies wrongdoing.
- Sánchez's ally, former prime minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero, is under a corruption investigation, which he denies. Sánchez's popularity has been further dented this year by a probe into alleged misuse of funds by the Socialist Party and a corruption investigation into Sánchez's ally, former Prime Minister José Luis Rodríguez Zapatero. Zapatero denies wrongdoing.

**Economy**
- The IMF raised its growth forecast for Spain. The October outlook lifts Spain's 2026 forecast by 0.4 points to 2.5%, above both the US and Germany.

**Sports**
- Real Madrid forward Vinicius Junior will miss El Clásico on October 25. He is serving a four-match ban for pulling Saliba's hair in La Liga.
- Spain was punished by FIFA for Islamophobic chants during an Egypt friendly.

**International and other news**
- Trump threatened to cut off Spanish trade and diplomatic relations.
- A Spanish NGO halted Mediterranean rescue operations, citing fuel prices.
- Health and weather: There was an urgent health alert in Spain after more than a dozen people were infected with salmonella from contaminated eggs.

The results are from October 4–18, 2026, so some details may have changed since then.

content.text:
Here are three of the biggest Spain stories from Oct 12–19, 2026:

1. **The snap election campaign is under way:** Pedro Sánchez called a general election for 29 November after Congress rejected his housing decrees amid mass protests, and this week parties formed alliances while housing stayed the main issue. ([The Olive Press, Oct 18](https://www.theolivepress.es/spain-news/2026/10/18/spain-political-roundup-october-18/); background on the Oct 5 announcement: [Euronews](https://www.euronews.com/2026/10/05/pedro-sanchez-calls-early-elections-in-spain-after-defeat-of-housing-decrees))

2. **The IMF raised Spain's growth forecast:** On Oct 13 it lifted Spain's 2026 forecast by 0.4 points to 2.5%, above both the US and Germany, which helps Sánchez heading into the vote. ([The Olive Press, Oct 13](https://www.theolivepress.es/spain-news/2026/10/13/spain-economic-growth-imf-forecast/))

3. **Madrid teachers began an open-ended strike:** Teachers in the Madrid region's public schools (below university level) went on strike on Oct 14 with no end date set. ([Infobae/EFE, Oct 14](https://www.infobae.com/espana/agencias/2026/10/13/temas-del-dia-de-efe-espana-del-miercoles-14-de-octubre-de-2026/))

The search results only go up to Oct 18, and "most important" is my own call. I left out a reported red rain warning in Valencia because I couldn't find another source to confirm it.
